gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many 8-hour coding days each board runs per charge with the backlight on: about 2 for the Lofree Flow 2 84 (17 h ÷ 8) against 7.5 to 12.5 for the NuPhy Air75 V3 (60 to 100 h ÷ 8), which puts the Flow 2's lit draw near 176 mA against 40 to 67 mA.
standout_why: Compared against mechkeyfoundry.com/best-low-profile-mechanical-keyboard-wireless (cited in chat 2), its Air75 V3 vs Flow 2 vs K3 Max page, and keeb-finder's K3 Max vs Air75 V2 page. Mechkeyfoundry already prints every raw input (4,000 mAh, 1,200 h off, 60-100 h on; 3,000 mAh, 120 h off, 17 h on; 1,500 mAh, 15 days on) and one derived figure, 'about a week of eight-hour days' for the Air75 V3. It gives no workday figure for the Flow 2, no implied draw, and says Keychron publishes no hour figure for the K3 Max. Keeb-finder gives mAh only. The two RTINGS pages (best low-profile, Air75 V2 review) returned only navigation to my fetch, so I could not check them. The rating is 1 because the new part is only the Flow 2 arithmetic and the draw comparison. It would be 2 if the K3 Max hour rating in 'unsourced' is confirmed on Keychron's page.
decides: Confirms the NuPhy Air75 V3 as the overall pick for a programmer who keeps the backlight on: 3.5 to 5.9 times the Flow 2's lit runtime (60 ÷ 17 to 100 ÷ 17). Our Lofree Flow 2 84 keeps the aluminum-body, typing-feel segment, with one condition to state: backlight off it lasts 15 workdays (120 h ÷ 8), backlight on it needs charging about every second day or running on USB-C. The Keychron K3 Max, the value and QMK pick, cannot be ranked on this figure until its hour rating is read from Keychron's page.

unsourced: Keychron K3 Max rated wireless hours. keychron.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt (WebFetch and storecheck.py), and keychron.com.au did the same. A search snippet attributed to Keychron's listing said 'Backlit off: around 73 hours; RGB: around 42 hours (lowest brightness)', and a PBTech NZ snippet said 78 h / 40 h. I opened neither page, so no value is reported. If Keychron's page confirms it, the derived figures would be 42 ÷ 8 = 5.25 lit workdays and 73 ÷ 8 = 9.1 unlit, and it would contradict mechkeyfoundry's 'no battery-life figure in hours'.
